🔖 Binance has confirmed that it is working closely with the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) and cryptocurrency industry partners to recover funds stolen during its October security breach, following the government’s latest action to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC. In a November 24 statement on X, the cryptocurrency exchange said it intends to remain involved throughout the asset forfeiture proceedings and is working with companies that have helped prevent the movement of stolen funds.

📊 “We are coordinating closely with the U.S. Department of Justice, as well as with industry partners who have assisted in freezing assets impacted by the incident,” Binance wrote. “We expect to continue cooperating throughout the asset forfeiture process, with the goal of supporting the return of affected funds as efficiently as possible.” The statement followed an announcement from the FBI’s Cyber Branch that U.S. authorities and private sector companies had collectively assisted in freezing, seizing or returning more than $2.9 billion in cryptocurrency since the October 29 theft.

⚠️ Circle Internet Financial, the issuer of USDC, had voluntarily restricted access to the funds before federal prosecutors obtained a court order. On November 6, Circle informed authorities that it would maintain the restrictions until the forfeiture proceedings concluded or the court instructed it otherwise, provided prosecutors obtained a temporary restraining order. The court subsequently granted an initial 14-day restraint. Alongside Monday’s forfeiture complaint, government attorneys submitted a request to keep the assets frozen throughout the legal proceedings.

🛡 Get paid safely: Clients Who Push You Off-Platform Mid-Deal

The trap: A client asks to finish payment via personal wallet or chat app after work starts, then vanishes once you deliver, leaving no record.

Do this
1. Insist on keeping all payment and messages inside the original platform until the job fully closes.
2. Ask the client why they want to move off-platform and treat vague answers as a warning sign.
3. If moving is unavoidable, get payment terms, amount, and wallet address confirmed in writing first.
4. Check the client's platform history and reviews before agreeing to any off-platform arrangement.

🚩 Stop if A client wants to discuss payment only through private chat right after the contract is agreed.

🔖 Save this. And keep the deal and the payment on the platform — that's what escrow is for.

Crypto Idea

Yesterday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge, together with Claude, presented a formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. It is one of the most famous mathematical problems in history, one that mathematicians have been unable to solve for 167 years.

In short, the Riemann Hypothesis describes a fundamental pattern in the distribution of prime numbers. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers $1 million for its solution.

The proof has not yet been officially accepted. However, the published materials have already undergone several serious independent technical reviews. If the mathematical community confirms the result, it would be a historic event.

But what matters more here is not the mathematics itself.

If AI really helped solve a problem in just a few weeks that generations of the world's best mathematicians had unsuccessfully worked on for more than a century and a half, it means we're approaching a point where artificial intelligence is beginning to do more than just use existing knowledge — it's starting to create new knowledge.

Now imagine that the next step happens within AI itself.

Today, solving some complex problem might require, say, 10,000 GPUs. Tomorrow, AI discovers a new algorithm that allows it to solve the same problem using 100 GPUs. Then 10. Then just one.

This is still a hypothetical scenario. But if AI really starts independently finding ways to radically improve the efficiency of its own computations, a huge portion of today's forecasts for data centers, energy, and chip demand could quickly become irrelevant.

We're currently building hundreds of billions of dollars' worth of infrastructure based on how much computing power today's technologies require.

But what if tomorrow's technology suddenly requires 100 or 1,000 times less?

And what would happen to all the investments that the market today considers almost guaranteed winners of the AI revolution?

Why are so many people missing out? The book keeps being taken off the market.
